Playground Chalk Calendar 010

Our class draws a big calendar on the covered playground. Each square is one day. We use white chalk for dates and yellow chalk for club times. On Tuesday, the chess club changes from Friday to Thursday. We rub out only its yellow words, not the date. Then we write the new time in Thursday’s square. The teacher asks us to copy the change onto the class noticeboard too. Children who do not pass the playground still need to know about it.

Class notice: Food collection for the community pantry
Please bring unopened, labelled food that can be stored without a fridge. Rice, dried beans and sealed tins are welcome. Do not bring home-cooked meals, opened packets or glass jars. Put food on the table outside Room 8, not in the school office. If you are unsure about an item, ask Ms Cole before bringing it. Families may also help by carrying boxes after school; donating food is not the only way to take part.

originalGroup.material:
Swimming Results Timing 010

At sports day, pupils swam the same short distance in two groups. The morning group used an electronic timer. After lunch, the device failed, so two teachers used hand-held stopwatches. The afternoon times appeared slightly slower. A pupil wanted to rank everyone in one list immediately.
The sports teacher explained that the distance had stayed the same but the timing method had changed. Small differences might come from how the stopwatches were started and stopped. It would be unfair to treat every tiny difference as certain proof of a faster swimmer.
The school displayed results in two sections and stated which method each used. Pupils with close times could join another supervised swim on a later day if they wanted a common comparison. Nobody had to repeat the swim to receive a participation certificate. The teacher said a result sheet should show both the measured numbers and enough information to understand them.
